## <a id="inseam_plugin_host_0_1_0"></a>Import interface inseam:plugin/host@0.1.0

Host capabilities, granted per the plugin's manifest. Calling a function
the manifest did not request (or whose budget is spent) returns an error
string; a well-behaved plugin degrades to doing less.

----

### Functions

#### <a id="log"></a>`log: func`

Diagnostic logging into the node's tracing output.

##### Params

- <a id="log.message"></a>`message`: `string`

#### <a id="llm_complete"></a>`llm-complete: func`

One metered LLM completion (requires the `llm` capability). Model
choice and budgeting belong to the host, not the plugin.

##### Params

- <a id="llm_complete.system"></a>`system`: `string`
- <a id="llm_complete.user"></a>`user`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="llm_complete.0"></a> result<`string`, `string`>

#### <a id="llm_describe_image"></a>`llm-describe-image: func`

One metered vision call: OCR, captioning (requires `llm`).

##### Params

- <a id="llm_describe_image.prompt"></a>`prompt`: `string`
- <a id="llm_describe_image.mimetype"></a>`mimetype`: `string`
- <a id="llm_describe_image.image"></a>`image`: list<`u8`>

##### Return values

- <a id="llm_describe_image.0"></a> result<`string`, `string`>

#### <a id="source_bytes"></a>`source-bytes: func`

The raw bytes of the claimed fragment (requires the `source-bytes`
capability): the source's own bytes at the root, or the content a
non-root fragment references (an image a document links to) when
the plugin claims non-roots too.

##### Return values

- <a id="source_bytes.0"></a> result<list<`u8`>, `string`>

## <a id="inseam_plugin_fetch_0_1_0"></a>Import interface inseam:plugin/fetch@0.1.0

The node's guarded HTTP request, performed on the component's behalf
(requires `[capabilities] hosts = [...]` — the manifest names every host
the plugin may contact, and the guard refuses everything else, redirect
hops included). The node owns the network stack: it resolves the host,
pins the connection, caps the body, and times the request out; the
component only describes the request.

----

### Types

#### <a id="request"></a>`record request`

One request to perform. `method` is one of GET, HEAD, POST, PUT,
PATCH, DELETE. Headers the transport owns (`host`,
`content-length`, ...) are refused. With `authorize`, the node
attaches the bearer token of the OAuth grant the entry names
(requires `[capabilities] grant = true`); the token itself never
crosses this boundary.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="request.method"></a>`method`: `string`
- <a id="request.url"></a>`url`: `string`
- <a id="request.headers"></a>`headers`: list<(`string`, `string`)>
- <a id="request.body"></a>`body`: option<list<`u8`>>
- <a id="request.authorize"></a>`authorize`: `bool`

#### <a id="response"></a>`record response`

The answer, status included: a non-success status is an answer a
plugin reads for itself, never an error. The body is under the
entry's byte cap.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="response.status"></a>`status`: `u16`
- <a id="response.headers"></a>`headers`: list<(`string`, `string`)>
- <a id="response.body"></a>`body`: list<`u8`>

----

### Functions

#### <a id="fetch"></a>`fetch: func`

Perform one request. Errors are the guard's refusals (a host the
manifest does not name, a private address, a spent call budget),
the network's, and the caps'.

##### Params

- <a id="fetch.request"></a>`request`: [`request`](#request)

##### Return values

- <a id="fetch.0"></a> result<[`response`](#response), `string`>

## <a id="inseam_plugin_connection_0_1_0"></a>Export interface inseam:plugin/connection@0.1.0

----

### Types

#### <a id="host_description"></a>`record host-description`

Which host this instance stewards, once configured.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="host_description.kind"></a>`kind`: `string`
  <p>The locator-schema family (`github`, `gmail`): lowercase ASCII,
  digits and `-`, at most 32 characters — the domain separator
  in host-id derivation.

- <a id="host_description.principal"></a>`principal`: `string`
  <p>The host's own identity (a repository, an account), never the
  protocol used to reach it. Trimmed and lowercased before
  hashing.

- <a id="host_description.display_name"></a>`display-name`: `string`
  <p>Owner-facing name.


#### <a id="edge_capabilities"></a>`record edge-capabilities`

What the edge supports. The bridge intersects these with the
manifest's declared capabilities — effective = declared AND
exported — so a component cannot declare itself writable past what
its manifest promised.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="edge_capabilities.enumerates"></a>`enumerates`: `bool`
- <a id="edge_capabilities.change_feed"></a>`change-feed`: `bool`
- <a id="edge_capabilities.writable"></a>`writable`: `bool`

#### <a id="content_length"></a>`variant content-length`

Content length as the envelope records it: lines for text, bytes
otherwise.

##### Variant Cases

- <a id="content_length.lines"></a>`lines`: `u64`
- <a id="content_length.bytes"></a>`bytes`: `u64`

#### <a id="envelope"></a>`record envelope`

A source's envelope, as the connection knows it. The bridge stamps
`observed` and validates `content-type` (an unparseable one becomes
`application/octet-stream`).

##### Record Fields

- <a id="envelope.source_type"></a>`source-type`: `string`
  <p>Plugin-level kind of source (`file`, `issue`); the vocabulary is
  the connection's.

- <a id="envelope.content_type"></a>`content-type`: `string`
- <a id="envelope.length"></a>`length`: [`content-length`](#content_length)
- <a id="envelope.created"></a>`created`: option<`s64`>
  <p>Unix-epoch seconds.

- <a id="envelope.modified"></a>`modified`: option<`s64`>
- <a id="envelope.hint"></a>`hint`: option<`string`>
  <p>Title-grade discovery hint.


#### <a id="source"></a>`record source`

One enumerated source: its locator on this host, its envelope, and
the raw byte size the sweep stores for change detection.

##### Record Fields

- <a id="source.locator"></a>`locator`: `string`
- <a id="source.envelope"></a>`envelope`: [`envelope`](#envelope)
- <a id="source.raw_bytes"></a>`raw-bytes`: `u64`

----

### Functions

#### <a id="configure"></a>`configure: func`

Receive the entry's plugin configuration (`[entry.config.plugin]`,
serialized as TOML) before anything else is asked. A configuration
the plugin cannot use is an error that fails the mount, named.

##### Params

- <a id="configure.config"></a>`config`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="configure.0"></a> result<_, `string`>

#### <a id="describe_host"></a>`describe-host: func`

The host this instance stewards. Asked once, after `configure`.

##### Return values

- <a id="describe_host.0"></a> result<[`host-description`](#host_description), `string`>

#### <a id="capabilities"></a>`capabilities: func`

What the edge supports. Asked once, after `configure`.

##### Return values

- <a id="capabilities.0"></a> [`edge-capabilities`](#edge_capabilities)

#### <a id="enumerate"></a>`enumerate: func`

Every enumerable source under `root`, a connection-interpreted scope
(a directory, a label, `""` for the whole host). Bounded by the
connection: an enumeration is one run's worth, never a stream.

##### Params

- <a id="enumerate.root"></a>`root`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="enumerate.0"></a> result<list<[`source`](#source)>, `string`>

#### <a id="locator_prefix"></a>`locator-prefix: func`

The locator prefix `root` covers, for reconciling vanished sources
(`""` says the whole host; none says the scope has no stable
prefix and reconciliation is skipped).

##### Params

- <a id="locator_prefix.root"></a>`root`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="locator_prefix.0"></a> option<`string`>

#### <a id="read_bytes"></a>`read-bytes: func`

The raw bytes of one source. Text sources serve their UTF-8; the
bridge derives text and line reads from these bytes.

##### Params

- <a id="read_bytes.locator"></a>`locator`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="read_bytes.0"></a> result<list<`u8`>, `string`>

#### <a id="describe"></a>`describe: func`

The envelope of one locator without enumerating. A host that only
learns envelopes by enumeration returns an error saying so.

##### Params

- <a id="describe.locator"></a>`locator`: `string`

##### Return values

- <a id="describe.0"></a> result<[`envelope`](#envelope), `string`>
